decisions.reason: As a close-to-core sensor module that extends the established modular platform, it is likely performing at least near aspiration and a growing firm with slack would usually retain it.
Its strong fit with the firm's industrial I/O architecture and earlier dedicated presentation suggest sufficiently good results relative to aspiration to justify continuation.

This relay module reuses existing capabilities and complements the installed base, so boundedly rational management would see little reason to reallocate resources away from it absent clear underperformance.
The server-room kit is somewhat more niche and solution-specific than the core modules, but in an expanding firm it would likely be kept unless sales had clearly fallen short of aspiration.
Because it was launched only recently and builds on the firm's controller-and-peripheral ecosystem, management would normally allow more time for learning before considering withdrawal.

Although a remote-access service carries more ongoing uncertainty than a hardware module, it fits the stated strategic push into wallbox and energy-management offerings and is therefore likely to be retained while results are assessed.
